description: Copper(II) ion in aqueous solution: broad, weak d-d transition absorption centred at ~810 nm (ε ~14 L·mol⁻¹·cm⁻¹) from the octahedral [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ complex. The blue colour is caused by this d→d transition (spin-allowed [²E₉→²T₂₉] in Oₕ field). A ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) band appears at ~300 nm.
transition: d→d crystal-field transition (²E₉ → ²T₂₉ in Oₕ symmetry) at 810 nm; LMCT at 300 nm
clinicalNote: Classic inorganic d-d transition example — demonstrates that d→d transitions have very low ε (~14) compared to organic chromophores (hundreds to hundreds of thousands). Used as copper deficiency treatment (Wilson’s disease antidote and agricultural fungicide).

sources.citation: Shriver DF, Atkins P (2006) Inorganic Chemistry, 4th ed., Oxford University Press. Chapter 20: d-d spectra of copper(II) complexes in aqueous solution; ε ≈ 14 at 810 nm.
sources.purpose: d-d transition λmax 810 nm and molar absorptivity ε ~14
